name: LAUGH AND LIE DOWN
description: Laugh and Lie Down is the earliest documented European fishing card game, dating back to 16th-century England. Played by five players, it is a game of capture where players aim to win pairs from a central pool. The game's name comes from its most famous mechanic: if a player cannot make a capture on their turn, they must discard their entire hand ('Lie Down') while the other players literally 'Laugh' at their misfortune.

content.text: Laugh and Lie Down is the earliest documented European fishing card game, dating back to 16th-century England. Played by five players, it is a game of capture where players aim to win pairs from a central pool. The game's name comes from its most famous mechanic: if a player cannot make a capture on their turn, they must discard their entire hand ('Lie Down') while the other players literally 'Laugh' at their misfortune.

First recorded in 1522 in a poem by John Skelton ('Why not to Court'). It is mentioned by Shakespeare and described in detail by Francis Willughby in his 17th-century 'Book of Games' (c. 1665), which is the only known historical description of the rules.
5 players is the standard historical format (Willughby's rules). Easily adapted for 3-6 players.
Standard 52-card deck. Ace is low for determining the dealer (lowest card deals).
Standard deck and counters for stakes.

Deal 8 cards to each player (one at a time, face down). Place the remaining 12 cards face-up on the table as the pool. The pool cards should be clearly visible but not arranged in any particular order.

items.text: Four Player Variant: Pot of 9p (3-2-2-2). Deal 10 each and 12 to the table. Last in hand wins 3p. Win/lose 1p per 2 cards above or below 10.
Three Player Variant: Pot of 10p (4-3-3). Deal 13 each and 13 to the table. Last in hand wins 5p. Win/lose 1p per 2 cards above or below 14.
Six Player Variant: Pot of 13p (3-2-2-2-2-2). Deal 7 each and 10 to the table. Last in hand wins 5p. Win/lose 1p per 2 cards above or below 6.
Tournament Version: Adaptation for tournament play with written scores. Mournivals go to eventual winner. Score 1 point per pair won in excess of original 8 cards.
